title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 103 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 539–542 (Night 103, continuing directly from nights-102), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 103 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Sharrukān, struck by Afrīdūn's lance, is carried back to the camp, and the battle rages until both armies are too weary to fight; in Constantinople King Ḥardūb hails Afrīdūn's victory. The wounded Sharrukān is tended through the night by the 'ascetic' — Dhāt al-Dawāhī in disguise — and recovers, crediting the ascetic's blessing. Next morning Ḍawʾ al-Makān rides out himself; Ḥardūb takes Afrīdūn's place and is beheaded, the vizier Dandān leads the Turks in a charge, and the Christians are driven back inside the city walls with heavy losses. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the third after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and third night,
sentences.n: “The third after the hundred”: the hundred and third night. The print spells miʾa “hundred” مائة, with an alif that is not pronounced.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ لَمَّارَأَى اللَّعِينَ قَدْ ضَرَبَ أَخَاهُ شَرْكَانَ بِالْحَرْبَةِ ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ مَاتَ فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِ الْفُرْسَانَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-malika ḍawʾa al-makāni lammā raʾā al-laʿīna qad ḍaraba akhāhu sharrukāna bi-al-ḥarbati ẓanna annahu māta fa-arsala ilayhi al-fursāna
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that King Ḍawʾ al-Makān, when he saw the accursed one had struck his brother Sharrukān with the spear, thought that he had died, and he sent to him the horsemen.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when King Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw that the accursed Afrīdūn had struck his brother Sharrukān with the lance, he thought him dead and sent horsemen to him.
sentences.n: The print runs words together twice here: السعيدان (al-saʿīdu anna) and لماراى (lammā raʾā). The spacing is kept as printed, and the pointing reads the words as they divide. “The accursed one” is Afrīdūn, who threw the lance at the end of the last night.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَسْبَقَ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَأَمِيرُ التُّرْكِ بَهْرَامُ وَأَمِيرُ الدَّيْلَمِ فَلَحِقُوهُ وَقَدْ مَالَ عَنْ جَوَادِهِ فَأَسْنَدُوهُ وَرَجَعُوا بِهِ إِلَى أَخِيهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna asbaqa al-nāsi ilayhi al-wazīru dandānu wa-amīru al-turki bahrāmu wa-amīru al-daylami fa-laḥiqūhu wa-qad māla ʿan jawādihi fa-asnadūhu wa-rajaʿū bihi ilā akhīhi ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: And the quickest of the people to him were the vizier Dandān and the emir of the Turks Bahrām and the emir of the Daylam; and they caught-up-with him, and he had leaned off his steed, and they propped him and returned with him to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: The first to reach him were the vizier Dandān, Bahrām the emir of the Turks, and the emir of the Daylamites. They came up with him as he was slipping from his horse, held him up, and brought him back to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.n: The print has اغيه, a misprint for اخيه (akhīhi, “his brother”), corrected here. Here the text calls Bahrām emir of the Turks and leaves the emir of the Daylamites unnamed; earlier in the tale the roles are the other way round (Bahrām leads the Daylam, Rustam the Turks). The storyteller has swapped them. As often, kāna stays singular before a compound subject (kāna asbaqa al-nāsi … al-wazīru dandānu wa-…): the verb agrees with the first name.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَوْصَوْابِهِ الْغِلْمَانَ وَعَادُوا إِلَى الْحَرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma awṣaw bihi al-ghilmāna wa-ʿādū ilā al-ḥarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni
sentences.l: Then they charged-with him the pages, and they went-back to the war and the lance-thrusting.
sentences.i: Then they left him in the care of the pages and went back to the war and the thrust of lances.
sentences.n: The print sets اوصوا به as one word, اوصوابه. awṣā bi-: to give someone a charge concerning someone, here “commend him to the pages’ care”; the bi- names the one being cared for.

sentences.t: وَاشْتَدَّ النِّزَالُ وَتَقَصَّفَتِ النِّصَالُ وَبَطَلَ الْقِيلُ وَالْقَالُ فَلَايُرَى إِلَّادَمٌ سَائِلٌ وَعُنُقٌ مَائِلٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ishtadda al-nizālu wa-taqaṣṣafati al-niṣālu wa-baṭala al-qīlu wa-al-qālu fa-lā yurā illā damun sāʾilun wa-ʿunuqun māʾilun
sentences.l: And the combat grew-fierce, and the blades shattered, and the said and the saying ceased, and there is not seen except blood flowing and a neck leaning.
sentences.i: The fighting grew fierce, blades broke to pieces, and all talk fell silent: nothing was to be seen but flowing blood and drooping necks.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: nizāl / niṣāl / qāl, then sāʾil / māʾil. al-qīl wa-al-qāl, “what is said and the saying”, is a set pair for chatter; when it ceases, the battle has passed beyond words. The print runs two pairs of words together, فلايرى (fa-lā yurā) and الّادم (illā damun); the shadda on الّا is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ السَّيْفُ يَعْمَلُ فِى الْأَعْنَاقِ وَاشْتَدَّ الشِّقَاقُ إِلَى أَنْ ذَهَبَ أَكْثَرُ اللَّيْلِ وَكَلَّتِ الطَّائِفَتَانِ عَنِ الْقِتَالِ فَنَادَوْا بِالِانْفِصَالِ وَرَجَعَتْ كُلُّ طَائِفَةٍ إِلَى خِيَامِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-sayfu yaʿmalu fī al-aʿnāqi wa-ishtadda al-shiqāqu ilā an dhahaba aktharu al-layli wa-kallati al-ṭāʾifatāni ʿani al-qitāli fa-nādaw bi-al-infiṣāli wa-rajaʿat kullu ṭāʾifatin ilā khiyāmihā
sentences.l: And the sword did not cease working in the necks, and the discord grew-fierce, until most of the night went, and the two parties grew-weary of the fighting, and they called for the separating, and every party returned to its tents.
sentences.i: The sword kept at its work among the necks and the strife grew bitter, until most of the night had gone and both sides were too weary to fight. Then they called for the armies to part, and each side went back to its tents.
sentences.n: nādaw bi-al-infiṣāl: “they called out the disengagement”, the bi- marking what is proclaimed. The shadda on كلّت is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَتَوَجَّهَ جَمِيعُ الْكُفَّارِ إِلَى مَلِكِهِمْ أَفْرِيدُونَ وَقَبَّلُّوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَهَنَّأَتْهُ الْقُسُوسُ وَالرُّهْبَانُ بِظَفَرِةِ بِشَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-tawajjaha jamīʿu al-kuffāri ilā malikihim afrīdūna wa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-hannaʾathu al-qusūsu wa-al-ruhbānu bi-ẓafarihi bi-sharrukāna
sentences.l: And all the unbelievers went to their king Afrīdūn and kissed the ground between his hands, and the priests and the monks congratulated him on his victory over Sharrukān.
sentences.i: All the unbelievers went to their king Afrīdūn and kissed the ground before him, and the priests and monks congratulated him on his victory over Sharrukān.
sentences.n: The print has وهنّأنه, a misprint for وهنّأته (hannaʾathu, “they congratulated him”: ن for ت), corrected here; the shadda is the print’s. The print also sets a shadda on the lām of قبلّوا rather than the bāʾ; it is kept where it stands, and the word is read qabbalū. In ظفرة the ة is written for the pronoun -hu: ẓafarihi, “his victory”. ẓafira bi-: to win over, get the better of; the second bi- names the one defeated.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَفْرِيدُونَ دَخَلَ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ مَمْلَكَتِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika afrīdūna dakhala al-qusṭanṭīniyyata wa-jalasa ʿalā kursiyyi mamlakatihi
sentences.l: Then indeed King Afrīdūn entered Constantinople and sat on the throne of his kingdom.
sentences.i: Then King Afrīdūn entered Constantinople and took his seat on the throne of his kingdom.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْمَلِكُ حَرْدُوبُ وَقَالَ لَهُ قَوَّى الْمَسِيحُ سَاعِدَكَ وَلَازَالَ مُسَاعِدَكَ وَاسْتَجَابَ مِنَ الْأُمِّ الصَّالِحَةِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي مَاتَدْعُو بِهِ لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbala ʿalayhi al-maliku ḥardūbu wa-qāla lahu qawwā al-masīḥu sāʿidaka wa-lā zāla musāʿidaka wa-istajāba mina al-ummi al-ṣāliḥati dhāti al-dawāhī mā tadʿū bihi laka
sentences.l: And King Ḥardūb came-forward to him and said to him: May the Messiah strengthen your forearm, and may he not cease your helper, and may he answer from the righteous mother Dhāt al-Dawāhī what she prays for you.
sentences.i: King Ḥardūb came to him and said: “May the Messiah strengthen your arm and never cease to be your helper, and may he grant whatever the holy mother Dhāt al-Dawāhī asks for you in her prayers.”
sentences.n: A play on two words from the same root: sāʿid, the forearm, the arm that strikes, and musāʿid, a helper. The perfect verbs qawwā, lā zāla and istajāba are wishes, as in a blessing. The print runs ولا زال and ما تدعو together (ولازال, ماتدعو). The shaddas on قوّى and الامّ are the print’s. Dhāt al-Dawāhī is in fact Ḥardūb’s own mother; “the righteous mother” is also a title for a holy woman.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مَابَقِيَ لَهُمْ إِقَامَةٌ بَعْدَ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam anna al-muslimīna mā baqiya lahum iqāmatun baʿda sharrukāna
sentences.l: And know that the Muslims, there has not remained for them a staying after Sharrukān.
sentences.i: “And know that, with Sharrukān gone, the Muslims cannot hold their ground.”
sentences.n: The print sets ما بقي as one word, مابقي. iqāma is “staying put”: the Muslims will not be able to keep up the siege.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَفْرِيدُونُ فِى غَدٍ يَكُونُ الِانْفِصَالُ إِذَا خَرَجْتُ إِلَى النِّزَالِ وَطَلَبْتُ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَقَتَلْتُهُ فَإِنَّ عَسْكَرَهُمْ يُوَلُّونَ الْأَدْبَارَ وَيَرْكَنُونَ إِلَى الْفِرَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla afrīdūnu fī ghadin yakūnu al-infiṣālu idhā kharajtu ilā al-nizāli wa-ṭalabtu ḍawʾa al-makāni wa-qataltuhu fa-inna ʿaskarahum yuwallūna al-adbāra wa-yarkanūna ilā al-firāri
sentences.l: And Afrīdūn said: Tomorrow will be the separating: when I go out to the combat and seek Ḍawʾ al-Makān and kill him, then their army will turn the backs and lean to the flight.
sentences.i: Afrīdūn said: “Tomorrow it will be settled. When I go out to fight and seek out Ḍawʾ al-Makān and kill him, their army will turn tail and take to flight.”
sentences.n: al-infiṣāl, the night’s “parting” of the armies, now means the decision of the war. ʿaskar “army” is singular, but the verbs that follow are plural: the soldiers, not the army, run. The shadda on يولّون is the print’s.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْكُفَّارِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri al-kuffāri
sentences.l: This is what was of the matter of the unbelievers.
sentences.i: So much for the unbelievers.
sentences.n: The storyteller’s formula for changing scene, completed by the “as for” (wa-ammā) that follows.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ عَسْكَرِ الْإِسْلَامِ فَإِنَّ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ لَمَّا رَجَعَ إِلَى الْخِيَامِ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شُغْلٌ إِلَّا بِأَخِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri ʿaskari al-islāmi fa-inna ḍawʾa al-makāni lammā rajaʿa ilā al-khiyāmi lam yakun lahu shughlun illā bi-akhīhi
sentences.l: And as for what was of the matter of the army of Islam: Ḍawʾ al-Makān, when he returned to the tents, there was not for him an occupation except with his brother.
sentences.i: As for the army of Islam: when Ḍawʾ al-Makān came back to the tents, he could think of nothing but his brother.
sentences.n: shughl bi-: being busy with someone; the bi- names what occupies him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَجَدَهُ فِي أَسْوَأِ الْأَحْوَالِ وَأَقَلِّ الْأَهْوَالِ فَدَعَا بِالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَرُسْتُمَ وَبَهْرَامَ لِلْمَشُورَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala ʿalayhi wajadahu fī aswaʾi al-aḥwāli wa-aqalli al-ahwāli fa-daʿā bi-al-wazīri dandāna wa-rustama wa-bahrāma li-al-mashūrati
sentences.l: And when he went in to him he found him in the worst of the states and the least of the terrors, and he called for the vizier Dandān and Rustam and Bahrām, for the counsel.
sentences.i: When he went in to him, he found him in the worst of states, and he sent for the vizier Dandān, Rustam and Bahrām to take counsel.
sentences.n: wa-aqalli al-ahwāli, “and the least of terrors”, is kept as printed but makes poor sense; it is there for the rhyme with al-aḥwāl, and the phrase may be corrupt (perhaps for ahwal al-ahwāl, “the most terrible of terrors”). The idiomatic layer leaves it out. daʿā bi-: “call for, summon”; the bi- marks the one sent for. The hamza on اسوأ is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ اقْتَضَى رَأْيُهُمْ إِحْضَارَ الْحُكَمَاءِ لِعِلَاجِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalū ʿalayhi iqtaḍā raʾyuhum iḥḍāra al-ḥukamāʾi li-ʿilāji sharrukāna
sentences.l: And when they went in to him, their opinion required the bringing of the physicians for the treating of Sharrukān.
sentences.i: When they came in to him, they agreed that physicians must be brought to treat Sharrukān.
sentences.n: The print has انتضى (intaḍā, “drew a sword”), a misprint for اقتضى (iqtaḍā, “required, called for”), corrected here. ḥakīm is “sage” and also “physician”; here the second.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَوْا وَقَالُوا لَمْ يَسْمَحْ بِمِثْلِهِ الزَّمَانُ وَسَهِرُوا عِنْدَهُ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma bakaw wa-qālū lam yasmaḥ bi-mithlihi al-zamānu wa-sahirū ʿindahu tilka al-laylata
sentences.l: Then they wept and said: Time has not been generous with his like; and they stayed-awake by him that night.
sentences.i: Then they wept and said, “Time has never granted the world another like him,” and they sat up with him all that night.
sentences.n: samaḥa bi-: to give freely, part with; the bi- names the gift. “Time has not been generous with his like”: there has never been anyone like him.

sentences.t: وَفِي آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِمُ الزَّاهِدُ وَهُوَ يَبْكِي فَلَمَّا رَآهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ قَامَ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī ākhiri al-layli aqbala ʿalayhimu al-zāhidu wa-huwa yabkī fa-lammā raʾāhu ḍawʾu al-makāni qāma ilayhi
sentences.l: And in the last of the night the ascetic came-forward to them, and he weeping; and when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw him he rose to him.
sentences.i: Toward the end of the night the ascetic came in to them, weeping, and when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw him he rose to meet him.
sentences.n: The “ascetic” is Dhāt al-Dawāhī in disguise, as the reader knows and the Muslims do not.

sentences.t: فَمَلَسَ بِيَدِهِ عَلَى جُرْحِ أَخِيهِ وَتَلَا شَيْأً مِنَ الْقُرْأَنِ وَعَوَّذَهُ بِآيَاتِ الرَّحْمٰنِ وَمَا زَالَ سَهْرَانًا عِنْدَهُ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-malasa bi-yadihi ʿalā jurḥi akhīhi wa-talā shayʾan mina al-qurʾāni wa-ʿawwadhahu bi-āyāti al-raḥmāni wa-mā zāla sahrānan ʿindahu ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And he stroked with his hand on the wound of his brother, and recited something of the Qurʾān, and charmed him with the verses of the Merciful, and he did not cease awake by him until the morning.
sentences.i: The ascetic passed his hand over Sharrukān’s wound, recited some of the Qurʾān, and said the verses of the Merciful over him as a protecting charm; and he stayed awake beside him until morning.
sentences.n: The subject here is the ascetic, and “his brother” is Ḍawʾ al-Makān’s. فملس is kept as printed and read malasa, “stroke, pass the hand smoothly”; it may be a slip for فلمس (fa-lamasa, “touched”). ʿawwadha: to recite protective verses over someone, the bi- naming the verses used. The dagger alif in الرحمٰن is the print’s, and so are the spellings شيأ and القرأن. sahrānan carries tanwīn as the print’s alif shows, though Classical usage would leave the word without it.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ اسْتَفَاقَ شَرْكَانُ وَفَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ وَأَدَارَلِسَانَهُ فِي فَمِهِ وَتَكَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika istafāqa sharrukānu wa-fataḥa ʿaynayhi wa-adāra lisānahu fī famihi wa-takallama
sentences.l: And at that, Sharrukān came-to, and opened his two eyes, and turned his tongue in his mouth and spoke.
sentences.i: At that Sharrukān came to himself, opened his eyes, moved his tongue in his mouth, and spoke.
sentences.n: The print sets ادار لسانه as one word, ادارلسانه.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ السُّلْطَانُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَقَالَ قَدْ حَصَلَ لَهُ بَرَكَةُ الزَّاهِدِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-sulṭānu ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-qāla qad ḥaṣala lahu barakatu al-zāhidi
sentences.l: And the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān rejoiced and said: The blessing of the ascetic has come to him.
sentences.i: Sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān was overjoyed. “The ascetic’s blessing has reached him,” he said.
sentences.n: ḥaṣala is masculine though baraka is feminine: a verb placed before its subject often stays in the masculine.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى الْعَافِيَةِ فَإِنَّنِي بِخَيْرٍ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ وَقَدْ عَمِلَ عَلَيَّ هَذَا الْمَلْعُونُ حِيلَةً وَلَوْلَا أَنِّي زُغْتُ أَسْرَعَ مِنَ الْبَرْقِ لَكَانَتِ الْحَرْبَةُ نَفَذَتْ مِنْ صَدْرِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu al-ḥamdu li-llāhi ʿalā al-ʿāfiyati fa-innanī bi-khayrin fī hādhihi al-sāʿati wa-qad ʿamila ʿalayya hādhā al-malʿūnu ḥīlatan wa-lawlā annī zughtu asraʿa mina al-barqi la-kānati al-ḥarbatu nafadhat min ṣadrī
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: Praise to God for the well-being, for I am in good at this hour; and this accursed one worked on me a trick, and were it not that I swerved quicker than the lightning, the spear would have gone-through from my chest.
sentences.i: Sharrukān said: “Praise be to God for my recovery; I am well now. That accursed man played a trick on me, and if I had not swerved faster than lightning, the lance would have gone right through my chest.”
sentences.n: zughtu, from zāgha, “turn aside, dodge”. ʿamila ʿalā … ḥīla: “work a trick on” someone. The shadda on عليّ is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي نَجَّانِي وَكَيْفَ حَالُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-al-ḥamdu li-llāhi alladhī najjānī wa-kayfa ḥālu al-muslimīna
sentences.l: So praise to God who saved me. And how is the state of the Muslims?
sentences.i: “Praise be to God, who saved me. And how are the Muslims?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ هُمْ فِي بُكَاءٍ مِنْ أَجْلِكَ فَقَالَ إِنِّي بِخَيْرٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ وَأَيْنَ الزَّاهِدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni hum fī bukāʾin min ajlika fa-qāla innī bi-khayrin wa-ʿāfiyatin wa-ayna al-zāhidu
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: They are in weeping on account of you. And he said: I am in good and well-being. And where is the ascetic?
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān told him, “They are all weeping for you.” He said, “I am well and whole. But where is the ascetic?”

sentences.t: وَكَانَ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ قَاعِدًا فَقَالَ لَهُ عِنْدَ رَأْسِكَ فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ʿinda raʾsihi qāʿidan fa-qāla lahu ʿinda raʾsika fa-iltafata ilayhi wa-qabbala yadayhi
sentences.l: And he was at his head, sitting. And he said to him: At your head. And he turned to him and kissed his two hands.
sentences.i: The ascetic was sitting by his head. “Right here, by your head,” his brother told him; and Sharrukān turned to him and kissed his hands.
sentences.n: The shadda on قبّل is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الزَّاهِدُ يَا وَلَدِي عَلَيْكَ بِجَمِيلِ الصَّبْرِ يُعْظِمِ اللَّهُ لَكَ الْأَجْرَ فَإِنَّ الْأَجْرَ عَلَى قَدْرِ الْمَشَقَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-zāhidu yā waladī ʿalayka bi-jamīli al-ṣabri yuʿẓimi allāhu laka al-ajra fa-inna al-ajra ʿalā qadri al-mashaqqati
sentences.l: And the ascetic said: O my son, upon you with the beautiful of the patience; God will make great for you the reward, for the reward is according to the measure of the hardship.
sentences.i: The ascetic said: “My son, hold fast to beautiful patience, and God will make your reward great, for the reward is in measure with the hardship.”
sentences.n: ʿalayka bi-: “hold to, take up”, an imperative idiom in which the bi- names what is to be held to. al-ṣabr al-jamīl, “beautiful patience”, is the Qurʾānic phrase for patience borne without complaint. yuʿẓimi is jussive, answering the command.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ ادْعُ لِي فَدَعَا لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu udʿu lī fa-daʿā lahu
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: Pray for me. And he prayed for him.
sentences.i: “Pray for me,” said Sharrukān, and he prayed for him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَبَانَ الْفَجْرُ وَلَاحَ بَرَزَتِ الْمُسْلِمُونَ إِلَى مَيْدَانِ الْحَرْبِ وَتَهَيَّأَ الْكُفَّارُ لِلطَّعْنِ وَالضَّرْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-bāna al-fajru wa-lāḥa barazati al-muslimūna ilā maydāni al-ḥarbi wa-tahayyaʾa al-kuffāru li-al-ṭaʿni wa-al-ḍarbi
sentences.l: And when the morning morninged and the dawn appeared and shone, the Muslims came-out to the field of the war, and the unbelievers made-ready for the thrusting and the striking.
sentences.i: When morning came and the dawn broke and shone, the Muslims marched out to the field of battle, and the unbelievers made ready to thrust and strike.
sentences.n: barazati al-muslimūna: a feminine verb with a masculine plural subject, a common loose agreement in this text. The shadda and hamza on تهيّأ are the print’s.

sentences.t: وَتَقَدَّمَتْ عَسَاكِرُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَطَلَبُوا الْحَرْبَ وَالْكِفَاحَ وَجَرَّدُوا السِّلَاحَ
sentences.tr: wa-taqaddamat ʿasākiru al-muslimīna fa-ṭalabū al-ḥarba wa-al-kifāḥa wa-jarradū al-silāḥa
sentences.l: And the armies of the Muslims advanced, and they sought the war and the hand-to-hand, and they bared the weapons.
sentences.i: The Muslim armies moved forward, seeking battle and close combat, with weapons drawn.
sentences.n: Rhyme: kifāḥ / silāḥ.

sentences.t: وَأَرَادَ الْمَلِكُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأَفْرِيدُونُ أَنْ يَحْمِلَا عَلَى بَعْضِهِمَا
sentences.tr: wa-arāda al-maliku ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-afrīdūnu an yaḥmilā ʿalā baʿḍihimā
sentences.l: And King Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Afrīdūn wanted that the two of them charge on one another.
sentences.i: King Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Afrīdūn each meant to charge the other.
sentences.n: ʿalā baʿḍihimā, “on each other”, literally “on some of the two of them”: a loose, everyday way of saying it.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ خَرَجَ إِلَى الْمَيْدَانِ وَخَرَجَ مَعَهُ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَالْحَاجِبُ وَبَهْرَامُ وَقَالُوا لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ نَحْنُ فِدَاكَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ḍawʾi al-makāni kharaja ilā al-maydāni wa-kharaja maʿahu al-wazīru dandānu wa-al-ḥājibu wa-bahrāmu wa-qālū li-ḍawʾi al-makāni naḥnu fidāka
sentences.l: And behold, Ḍawʾ al-Makān went-out to the field, and there went out with him the vizier Dandān and the chamberlain and Bahrām, and they said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: We are your ransom.
sentences.i: And there was Ḍawʾ al-Makān riding out onto the field, and with him the vizier Dandān, the chamberlain and Bahrām. “We will give our lives for yours,” they told him.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-: “and behold”; after idhā of surprise the bi- only marks who appears. naḥnu fidāka, “we are your ransom”: let us be killed in your place. They are asking him to stay back and let them fight.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ وَحَقِّ الْبَيْتِ الْحَرَامِ وَزَمْزَمَ وَالْمَقَامِ لَا أَقْعُدُ عَنِ الْخُرُوجِ إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ الْعُلُوجِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum wa-ḥaqqi al-bayti al-ḥarāmi wa-zamzama wa-al-maqāmi lā aqʿudu ʿani al-khurūji ilā hāʾulāʾi al-ʿulūji
sentences.l: And he said to them: By the right of the Sacred House and Zamzam and the Station, I will not sit back from the going-out to these barbarians.
sentences.i: He answered: “By the Sacred House, by Zamzam and the Station of Abraham, I will not hang back from going out against these infidel louts.”
sentences.n: The oath names the holy places of Mecca: the Kaʿba (“the Sacred House”), the well of Zamzam, and the Station of Abraham beside the Kaʿba. ʿulūj (sg. ʿilj) is a coarse word for non-Arab unbelievers, “boors, barbarians”. Rhyme: khurūj / ʿulūj.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا صَارَ فِى الْمَيْدَانِ لَعِبَ بِالسَّيْفِ وَالسِّنَانِ حَتَّى أَذْهَلَ الْفُرْسَانَ وَتَعَجَّبَ الْفَرِيقَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṣāra fī al-maydāni laʿiba bi-al-sayfi wa-al-sināni ḥattā adhhala al-fursāna wa-taʿajjaba al-farīqāni
sentences.l: And when he was in the field, he played with the sword and the spearhead until he astounded the horsemen, and the two sides marvelled.
sentences.i: Once he was on the field he made such play with sword and lance that the horsemen were dumbfounded and both armies marvelled.
sentences.n: laʿiba bi-: “play with, wield in display”; the bi- marks the weapons. Rhyme: maydān / sinān / fursān / farīqān.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلَ فِى الْمَيْمَنَةِ فَقَتَلَ مِنْهَا بِطْرِيقَيْنِ وَفِى الْمَيْسَرَةِ فَقَتَلَ مِنْهَا بِطْرِيقَيْنِ وَوَقَفَ فِي وَسَطِ الْمَيْدَانِ وَقَالَ أَيْنَ أَفْرِيدُونُ حَتَّي أُذِيقَهُ عَذَابَ الْهُونِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamala fī al-maymanati fa-qatala minhā biṭrīqayni wa-fī al-maysarati fa-qatala minhā biṭrīqayni wa-waqafa fī wasaṭi al-maydāni wa-qāla ayna afrīdūnu ḥattā udhīqahu ʿadhāba al-hūni
sentences.l: And he charged into the right wing and killed of it two patricians, and into the left wing and killed of it two patricians, and he stood in the middle of the field and said: Where is Afrīdūn, so that I make him taste the torment of the humiliation?
sentences.i: He charged into the enemy’s right wing and killed two patricians there, and into the left and killed two more; then he halted in the middle of the field and cried, “Where is Afrīdūn? Let me make him taste the torment of disgrace!”
sentences.n: ʿadhāb al-hūn, “the torment of humiliation”, is a Qurʾānic phrase. The print spells ḥattā with ي, حتي.

sentences.t: فَأَرَادَ الْمَلْعُونُ أَنْ يُوَلِّيَ وَهُوَ مَغْبُونٌ
sentences.tr: fa-arāda al-malʿūnu an yuwalliya wa-huwa maghbūnun
sentences.l: And the accursed one wanted to turn-away, he being cheated.
sentences.i: The accursed man would have turned away, outmatched.
sentences.n: maghbūn: “cheated, getting the worse of a bargain”; here, knowing he is beaten. It rhymes with al-hūn.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ الْمَلِكُ حَرْدُوبُ هَذَا الْحَالَ أَقْسَمَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ لَا يَخْرُجَ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا مَلِكُ بِالْأَمْسِ كَانَ قِتَالُكَ وَالْيَوْمَ قِتَالِي وَأَنَا بِشَجَاعَتِهِ لَا أُبَالِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu al-maliku ḥardūbu hādhā al-ḥāla aqsama ʿalayhi an lā yakhruja ilayhi wa-qāla lahu yā maliku bi-al-amsi kāna qitāluka wa-al-yawma qitālī wa-anā bi-shajāʿatihi lā ubālī
sentences.l: And when King Ḥardūb saw him this state, he swore upon him that he not go out to him, and he said to him: O king, yesterday was your fighting, and today my fighting, and I, for his courage I do not care.
sentences.i: When King Ḥardūb saw him in this state, he adjured him not to go out against him. “O king,” he said, “yesterday the fighting was yours, today it is mine; and I care nothing for his courage.”
sentences.n: aqsama ʿalayhi: “adjured him”, bound him by an oath not to go. bi-al-amsi, “yesterday”: the bi- marks the time. lā ubālī bi-: “not care about”; the verb takes bi- for what one does not care about. Rhyme: qitālī / ubālī.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجَ وَفِي يَدِهِ صَارِمٌ وَتَحْتَهُ حِصَانٌ كَأَنَّهُ الْأَبْجَرُ الَّذِي كَانَ لِعَنْتَرٍ وَذَلِكَ الْحِصَانُ أَدْهَمُ مُغَائِرٌ كَمَا قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: thumma kharaja wa-fī yadihi ṣārimun wa-taḥtahu ḥiṣānun ka-annahu al-abjaru alladhī kāna li-ʿantarin wa-dhālika al-ḥiṣānu adhamu mughāʾirun kamā qāla al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: Then he went out, and in his hand a cutting-sword, and under him a stallion as if it were al-Abjar, which was ʿAntar’s, and that stallion black, unmatched, as the poet said:
sentences.i: Then he rode out, a keen sword in his hand and under him a stallion like al-Abjar, the horse of ʿAntar: a black horse without its equal, as the poet says:
sentences.n: al-Abjar was the horse of ʿAntara ibn Shaddād, the warrior-poet of pre-Islamic Arabia and hero of a long popular romance; the print gives the name as ʿAntar, as the romance does. ṣārim, “cutting”, is a stock word for a sword. مغائر is kept as printed and doubtful: it is read mughāʾir, taken as mughāyir, “different, unlike others”; the sense is uncertain.

sentences.t:
قَدْ سَابَقَ الطَّرْفَ بِطِرْفٍ سَابِقٍ * كَاَنَّهُ يُرِيدُ اِدْرَاكَ الْقَدَرْ
دُهْمَتُهُ تُبْدِي سَوَادًا حَالِكًا * كَاَنَّهَا لَيْلٌ اِذَا اللَّيْلُ عَكَرْ
صَهِيلُهُ يُطْرِبُ مَنْ يَسْمَعُهُ * كَاَنَّهُ الرَّعْدُ اِذَا الرَّعْدُ زَجَرْ
لَوْسَابَقَ الرِّيحَ جَرَى مِنْ قَبْلِهَا * وَالْبَرْقُ لَا يُسْبِقُهُ اِذَا ظَهَرْ
sentences.tr:
qad sābaqa al-ṭarfa bi-ṭirfin sābiqin * ka-annahu yurīdu idrāka al-qadar
duhmatuhu tubdī sawādan ḥālikan * ka-annahā laylun idhā al-laylu ʿakar
ṣahīluhu yuṭribu man yasmaʿuhu * ka-annahu al-raʿdu idhā al-raʿdu zajar
law sābaqa al-rīḥa jarā min qablihā * wa-al-barqu lā yusbiquhu idhā ẓahar
sentences.n: Verse, as printed with its own pointing. The first line plays on ṭarf, “glance of the eye”, and ṭirf, “a thoroughbred horse”, two words written alike. The print runs لو سابق together (لَوْسَابَقَ), and points يُسْبِقُهُ as a fourth-form verb, where yasbiquhu, “outstrips it”, is expected; both are kept as printed. Each line ends in a pausal form without its final vowel: al-qadar, ʿakar, zajar, ẓahar.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَمَلَ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ وَاحْتَرَزَ مِنْ مَضَارِبِهِ وَأَظْهَرَ مَا فِي بَطْنِهِ مِنْ عَجَائِبِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥamala kullun minhumā ʿalā ṣāḥibihi wa-iḥtaraza min maḍāribihi wa-aẓhara mā fī baṭnihi min ʿajāʾibihi
sentences.l: Then each of the two charged upon his fellow, and guarded himself from his strokes, and showed what was in his belly of his wonders.
sentences.i: Then each charged the other, guarding against his blows and bringing out every marvel of skill he had in him.
sentences.n: “What was in his belly”: whatever he had inside him, all his hidden skill. Rhyme: ṣāḥibihi / maḍāribihi / ʿajāʾibihi. The two fighters are now Ḍawʾ al-Makān and King Ḥardūb.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَا فِى الْكَرِّ وَالْفَرِّ حَتَّى ضَاقَتِ الصُّدُورُ وَقَلَّ الصَّبْرُ لِلْمَقْدُورِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhā fī al-karri wa-al-farri ḥattā ḍāqati al-ṣudūru wa-qalla al-ṣabru li-al-maqdūri
sentences.l: And the two of them took-to the attacking and the withdrawing, until the breasts were straitened and the patience grew little for the decreed.
sentences.i: They wheeled to attack and fell back again, until hearts grew tight and there was little patience left for whatever fate had decreed.
sentences.n: akhadha fī: “set about, begin”. al-karr wa-al-farr, charge and retreat, is the set phrase for the back-and-forth of mounted combat; the shaddas on الكرّ and الفرّ are the print’s.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَهَجَمَ عَلَى مَلِكِ الْأَرْمَنِ حَرْدُوبَ وَضَرَبَهُ ضَرْبَةً أَطَاحَ بِهَا رَأْسَهُ وَقَطَعَ أَنْفَاسَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-hajama ʿalā maliki al-armani ḥardūba wa-ḍarabahu ḍarbatan aṭāḥa bihā raʾsahu wa-qaṭaʿa anfāsahu
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān shouted, and rushed upon the king of the Armenians, Ḥardūb, and struck him a stroke with which he sent-flying his head and cut his breaths.
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān gave a shout and fell on Ḥardūb, king of the Armenians, and dealt him a blow that sent his head flying and cut off his breath.
sentences.n: aṭāḥa bihā: “sent flying with it”; the bi- is the instrument, the stroke. Rhyme: raʾsahu / anfāsahu. Elsewhere in the tale Ḥardūb is king of the Rūm; only here does the storyteller call him king of the Armenians.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتِ الْكُفَّارُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ حَمَلُوا جَمِيعًا عَلَيْهِ وَتَوَجَّهُوا بِكُلِّيَّتِهِمْ إِلَيْهِ فَقَابَلَهُمْ فِي حَوْمَةِ الْمَيْدَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarati al-kuffāru ilā dhālika ḥamalū jamīʿan ʿalayhi wa-tawajjahū bi-kulliyyatihim ilayhi fa-qābalahum fī ḥawmati al-maydāni
sentences.l: And when the unbelievers looked at that, they charged all-together upon him, and turned with their entirety to him, and he met them in the thick of the field.
sentences.i: When the unbelievers saw this, they charged him all at once, turning their whole force against him, and he met them in the thick of the field.
sentences.n: bi-kulliyyatihim, “with the whole of them”; the bi- is “with”, of what they brought to bear. The shadda on بكلّيتهم is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَمَرَّ الضَّرْبُ وَالطِّعَانُ حَتَّى سَالَ الدَّمُ بِالْجَرَيَانِ وَضَجَّ الْمُسْلِمُونَ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ وَالتَّهْلِيلِ وَالصَّلٰوةِ عَلَى الْبَشِيرِ النَّذِيرِ
sentences.tr: wa-istamarra al-ḍarbu wa-al-ṭiʿānu ḥattā sāla al-damu bi-al-jarayāni wa-ḍajja al-muslimūna bi-al-takbīri wa-al-tahlīli wa-al-ṣalāti ʿalā al-bashīri al-nadhīri
sentences.l: And the striking and the thrusting went on until the blood flowed with the running, and the Muslims clamoured with the takbīr and the tahlīl and the blessing upon the bringer-of-good-tidings, the warner.
sentences.i: The cutting and thrusting went on until the blood ran in streams, and the Muslims raised a clamour of “God is greatest” and “There is no god but God”, and called down blessings on the Bearer of Good News and Warner.
sentences.n: takbīr is crying Allāhu akbar, “God is greatest”; tahlīl is crying lā ilāha illā allāh, “there is no god but God”. “The bringer of good tidings and the warner” is the Prophet, in Qurʾānic words. ḍajja bi-: “clamour with”; the bi- marks the cries. The print spells ṣalāt with wāw, الصلوة.

sentences.t: وَقٰتَلُوا قِتَالًا شَدِيدًا وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ النَّصْرَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْخِزْيَ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-qātalū qitālan shadīdan wa-anzala allāhu al-naṣra ʿalā al-muʾminīna wa-al-khizya ʿalā al-kāfirīna
sentences.l: And they fought a fighting fierce, and God sent down the victory upon the believers and the shame upon the unbelievers.
sentences.i: They fought fiercely, and God sent down victory on the believers and disgrace on the unbelievers.
sentences.n: The print writes قتلوا, which on its own would be qatalū, “they killed”; with qitālan after it the verb is qātalū, “fought”, written without its long alif, and the pointing supplies a dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ خُذُوا بِثَائِرِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَثَارِ وَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa al-wazīru dandānu khudhū bi-thāʾiri al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni wa-thāri waladihi sharrukāna
sentences.l: And the vizier Dandān shouted: Take the vengeance of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān and the vengeance of his son Sharrukān!
sentences.i: The vizier Dandān shouted: “Take vengeance for King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān and for his son Sharrukān!”
sentences.n: akhadha bi-thaʾr: “to exact blood-revenge for” someone; the bi- belongs to the idiom. The print writes thaʾr two ways in one breath: بثائر, kept as printed and read bi-thāʾiri (where bi-thaʾri is expected), and ثار, without its hamza. Sharrukān is not dead, but the vizier calls for revenge for the wound he took.

sentences.t: وَكَشَفَ رَأْسَهُ وَصَاحَ لِلْأَتْرَاكِ وَكَانَ بِجَانِبِهِ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ عِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ فَحَمَلُوا مَعَهُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً
sentences.tr: wa-kashafa raʾsahu wa-ṣāḥa li-al-atrāki wa-kāna bi-jānibihi aktharu min ʿishrīna alfa fārisin fa-ḥamalū maʿahu jumlatan wāḥidatan
sentences.l: And he uncovered his head and shouted to the Turks, and there was at his side more than twenty thousand horsemen, and they charged with him as one whole.
sentences.i: He bared his head and called to the Turks; there were more than twenty thousand horsemen at his side, and they charged with him as one.
sentences.n: Baring the head is a gesture of urgency and of readiness to die, rousing the men. li-al-atrāk: li- “to”, of those he calls.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَجِدِ الْكُفَّارُ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ غَيْرَ الْفِرَارِ وَتَوَلَّى الْأَدْبَارَ وَعَمِلَ فِيهِمُ الصَّارِمُ الْبَتَّارُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yajidi al-kuffāru li-anfusihim ghayra al-firāri wa-tawallā al-adbāra wa-ʿamila fīhimu al-ṣārimu al-battāru
sentences.l: And the unbelievers did not find for themselves other than the flight, and turned the backs, and the sharp, the cutting sword worked among them.
sentences.i: The unbelievers found nothing left for themselves but flight; they turned their backs, and the keen and cutting sword went to work among them.
sentences.n: tawallā is singular though its subject, the unbelievers, is plural: the storyteller treats them as one body. Rhyme: firār / battār.

sentences.t: فَقَتَلُوا مِنْهُمْ نَحْوَ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ وَأَسَرُوا مَا يَزِيدُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَقُتِلَ عِنْدَ دُخُولِ الْبَابِ خَلْقٌ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الزِّحَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qatalū minhum naḥwa khamsīna alfa fārisin wa-asarū mā yazīdu ʿalā dhālika wa-qutila ʿinda dukhūli al-bābi khalqun kathīrun min shiddati al-ziḥāmi
sentences.l: And they killed of them about fifty thousand horsemen and captured what exceeds that, and there was killed at the entering of the gate a great creation from the severity of the crush.
sentences.i: They killed some fifty thousand of their horsemen and took more than that number prisoner, and a great many were killed at the gate as they crowded to get in.
sentences.n: The ḍamma on قُتل is the print’s, marking the passive.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ غَلَّقَ الرُّومُ الْبَابَ وَطَلَعُوا فَوْقَ الْأَسْوَارِ خَوْفَ الْعَذَابِ
sentences.tr: thumma ghallaqa al-rūmu al-bāba wa-ṭalaʿū fawqa al-aswāri khawfa al-ʿadhābi
sentences.l: Then the Rūm shut the gate and went up on top of the walls, for fear of the torment.
sentences.i: Then the Greeks shut the gate and climbed up onto the walls, fearing the punishment to come.
sentences.n: al-Rūm are the Byzantine Greeks. ghallaqa, “shut fast”, is pointed as the second form; the print’s letters also allow ghalaqa, a colloquial form of the same verb.

sentences.t: وَعَادَتْ طَوَائِفُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مُؤَيَّدِينَ مَنْصُورِينَ وَأَتَوْاخِيَا مَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿādat ṭawāʾifu al-muslimīna muʾayyadīna manṣūrīna wa-ataw khiyāmahum
sentences.l: And the bands of the Muslims returned, aided, made-victorious, and came to their tents.
sentences.i: The Muslim companies came back strengthened by God and victorious, and returned to their tents.
sentences.n: The print divides وأتوا خيامهم (“and they came to their tents”) in the wrong place, as واتواخيا مهم; the spacing is kept and the pointing reads across it. muʾayyad: “supported” by God.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ الْمَلِكُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ عَلَى أَخِيهِ فَوَجَدَهُ فِي أَسَرِّ الْأَحْوَالِ فَسَجَدَ شُكْراً لِلْكَرِيمِ الْمُتَعَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala al-maliku ḍawʾu al-makāni ʿalā akhīhi fa-wajadahu fī asarri al-aḥwāli fa-sajada shukran li-al-karīmi al-mutaʿāli
sentences.l: And King Ḍawʾ al-Makān went in to his brother and found him in the most joyful of the states, and he prostrated in thanks to the Generous, the Exalted.
sentences.i: King Ḍawʾ al-Makān went in to his brother and found him in the best of spirits, and he bowed down in thanks to the Generous, the Most High.
sentences.n: asarr al-aḥwāl, “the most joyful of states”, answers aswaʾ al-aḥwāl, “the worst of states”, earlier in this night. li-al-karīm: li- “to”, of the one thanked. The shadda on اسرّ and the tanwīn on شكراً are the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَنَّأَهُ بِالسَّلَامَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ شَرْكَانُ إِنَّنَا كُلَّنَا فِي بَرَكَةِ هَذَا الزَّاهِدِ الْأَوَّابِ وَمَا انْتَصَرْتُمْ إِلَّابِدُعَائِهِ الْمُسْتَجَابِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala ʿalayhi wa-hannaʾahu bi-al-salāmati fa-qāla lahu sharrukānu innanā kullanā fī barakati hādhā al-zāhidi al-awwābi wa-mā intaṣartum illā bi-duʿāʾihi al-mustajābi
sentences.l: Then he came to him and congratulated him on the safety, and Sharrukān said to him: We, all of us, are in the blessing of this ascetic, the oft-returning, and you did not win except by his prayer, the answered.
sentences.i: Then he came up to him and congratulated him on his recovery. Sharrukān said: “We all live by the blessing of this penitent ascetic. You won only because his prayer was answered.”
sentences.n: hannaʾa bi-: “congratulate on”; the bi- names the occasion. awwāb, “one who turns back to God often”, is a Qurʾānic word of praise. The irony is the storyteller’s: the “ascetic” is the enemy’s own agent. The print runs الا بدعائه together (الابدعائه). The shaddas on هنّأه and الاوّاب are the print’s.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَزَلِ الْيَوْمَ قَاعِدًا يَدْعُو لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ بِالنَّصْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu lam yazali al-yawma qāʿidan yadʿū li-al-muslimīna bi-al-naṣri
sentences.l: For he did not cease today sitting, praying for the Muslims for the victory.
sentences.i: “He sat all day long praying for the Muslims to win.”
sentences.n: daʿā li-… bi-: “pray for someone (li-) to have something (bi-)”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The print has المباج, a misprint for المباح (al-mubāḥ, “permitted”), corrected here.
